newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BAD LANGUAGE FOLLOWS BAD LIGHT AT ESSEX.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BAD LANGUAGE FOLLOWS BAD LIGHT AT ESSEX.

text.p: Tempers flared between Essex fast bowler Mark Ilott and Glamorgan's England off-spinner Robert Croft on Tuesday as bad light stopped play in their Natwest Trophy semifinal with Essex needing six runs to win.
The two jostled and traded insults at close quarters after the Essex batsman complained about the poor visibility.
Play was called off shortly after 8 p.m. after Glamorgan fast bowler Waqar Younis had delivered one ball of the 54th over.
Essex were on 296 for eight, chasing Glamorgan's 301 for eight made off the full 60 overs.
The match resumes on Wednesday with Essex set to reach their second successive NatWest final, against Warwickshire or Sussex at Lord's on September 6.
Warwickshire and Sussex play at Edgbaston on Wednesday.
Ronnie Irani, battling on under painkillers for injured rib muscles, helped Essex to the verge of victory with a battling 51 before leaving lbw to pace bowler Darren Thomas.
